title: Rockhead refuses Butler as leader; matinee success in full dress
summary: Rockhead insisted a Canadian lead; Butler wrote the music, had the band wear full dress, and the French-language matinee with a French theme song was a hit.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: Freddie was -- and the scars was in his memory. He was scarred. Very scarred. But he liked me and so he say, Mr. Rockhead says, well, Jacques can lead the band. He said, Jacques is no Canadian, we are Canadian, we don't want him to lead no band." And went into a frantic scene.

And I said, well, I didn't come to lead no band, Mr. Rockhead. I can write the music for the band and I don't have to lead it. I said, well, let Bill lead it. He say, I don't know about leading no band and I said, well, he's the leader -- at least --
I got the band together and I consulted to find out what the people liked because you see we got the French population there so I got a -- I put them all in full dress on Sunday.
They was just -- we had a matinee and Scotty's there /and I said fellows, now, you are going to catch them by urprise. When they see you, they, that's it.
So, and we rehearsed and rehearsed and we got the numbers all together, singing, and everything then we had a few French songs and we had a theme song that was a French

song.
And we did a matinee, that was, everybody was there
to see the matinee and when we opened up with the theme
song, there was, it was raining out then -- hands --

So, we were a success. Freddie says Jacques, I
love you. I said, yeah, Freddie, I know. I heard that
love. I heard all of that love.
